correctness.rationale: Orthogonalizing against 1 gives K(s,t)=1+(u(s)-m)(u(t)-m)/v with u(t)=exp(-lambda t). Convexity in u(s) reduces the absolute row integral to the two endpoints; a sign test attains it there. The strictly positive mean of (1-u)(u-q) gives v<(1-m)(m-q), so the monotone endpoint rows cross once with the asserted root ordering and opposite signs at t=0. Their primitives give the displayed branches. Since the signed row mass is 1, an indicator of the negative part attains the most negative output over data in [0,1]; this is the sharp lower value meant by the negative-overshoot wording. For the small-rate check, the equivalent basis function g=(1-u)/lambda has mean 1/2-lambda/6+O(lambda^2) and variance 1/12-lambda/12+O(lambda^2). Substitution gives the frozen endpoint-row corrections 3t^2-4t+1 and 2t-3t^2; integrating with the signs at the simple limiting zeros 2/3 and 1/3 gives derivatives 4/27 and -4/27. The shifted sign intervals affect the expansions only at O(lambda^2). At large rate k_+=2lambda+2+O(1/lambda), 1-k_+m=-1-2/lambda+O(lambda^-2), and z_+=1/(2lambda)+O(lambda^-2). Thus the zero is at log(2lambda)/lambda+O(lambda^-2) and (k_+/lambda)(1-z_+)=2+1/lambda+O(lambda^-2), yielding exactly the stated norm correction. The other row is 1+O(1/lambda), so only the first row matters in this limit. No all-rate branch dominance is needed.
residual_risks: The reported supplementary checks were not replayed or used to certify the analytic statements. Frozen expert, independent-audit and Lean channels are marked not performed.

evidence: Kayumov gives a sharp partition-uniform bound of 3 for symmetric opposite-sign exponents, and a uniform-in-partition bound for unequal strictly opposite-sign exponents. The two least-squares papers treat polynomial projection on spheres with sampling/quadrature; Xu treats perturbation of finite-dimensional L2 projections.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A mesh-uniform supremum or general kernel norm representation does not give the finite-interval, zero-exponent rate corrections or zero locations. Conjugation by multiplication to shift exponents is not an unweighted L2 or L∞ isometry.

evidence: The affine formulation after x=exp(-lambda t) uses the normalized measure dx/(lambda x) on [exp(-lambda),1]. The affine-Jacobi hit has symmetric Dirichlet weights on a simplex and a dimension limit, not this measure. The two-rate hit has two strictly decaying modes on the half-line, with norm 4(R+1)R^(-1-1/(R-1)).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The change of variables to the log-uniform measure preserves the endpoint norm; replacing that law by uniform, Dirichlet, or by the unweighted half-line changes the projection. A coincident value of 3 is not equivalence.

value.rationale: The exact amplification of uniformly bounded data and the exact loss of positivity concern a natural two-mode least-squares model. The comparison of nearly coalescing modes with rapid decay separates a polynomial-limit sensitivity from a logarithmic correction and locates the row sign change. These are quantitative facts unavailable from just a generic kernel estimate or the limiting constant.
residual_risks: No conclusion about optimal projections, other sampling laws, or larger exponential families.
